title: The Cold Colony Revisited
premise: Beatrix Crane smuggles memories between the warring worlds of Meridian and Halcyon, staying neutral by never asking what she carries. When gravity fails system-wide for nine seconds, she discovers her latest cargo contains a dead courier's final memory: proof that both governments' war was manufactured by the orbital Authority that governs them all. Hunted by Authority enforcers and betrayed by the handler who raised her, Beatrix must choose between broadcasting the truth to both worlds — ending the war but destroying her own buried identity as the Authority's lost daughter — or selling it back and staying invisible. She broadcasts it, at the cost of everything, and the nine seconds of silence become the moment both worlds remember who their real enemy is.
about_author: August Iversen is a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade listening to conversations between ships that were never supposed to talk. They write about people who carry messages across borders that would rather stay closed.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Mid-run between worlds, gravity flickers for exactly nine seconds; Beatrix floats with her cargo hold open, watching a lifetime of carefully hidden contraband drift like snow. The beat is vertigo — the universe itself has broken its promise of constancy, and her invisibility along with it.

chapters.title: The Weight of What We Carry
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Docking at neutral station Vesper's Rest, she inspects the damaged cargo and finds one memory-chip encrypted in a code she almost recognizes. Her handler, Odile, summons her with unusual urgency. Beat: unease sharpening into dread as routine curdles into conspiracy.

chapters.title: What the Dead Courier Knew
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix, with an interlude from the dead courier's recorded memory. Decrypted, the chip shows the first bombardment of the war was ordered by the Authority itself — staged to justify orbital control. Beat: the sickening clarity of someone whose neutrality was always someone else's design.

chapters.title: Odile
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Confrontation with her handler reveals Odile has known for years and has been feeding Beatrix's routes to the Authority. But Odile hesitates — a flicker of the woman who once saved her. Beat: betrayal braided with love, and the first hint that Beatrix's past is not what she believes.

chapters.title: The Daughter of the Spire
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Chased through Vesper's Rest by Authority enforcers, she uncovers records showing she was born inside the Authority: the Director's daughter, memory-wiped and exiled after refusing to sign the war order. Beat: identity collapse — the smuggler discovers she was built to be a weapon and chose to forget.

chapters.title: Both Sides of the Dark
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Meridian gunner Elio Vasquez and Halcyon archivist Sena Okonkwo, strangers on opposite sides who each receive fragments of the leaked memory through pirate channels. Beat: parallel awakening — two enemies realizing they mourn the same fabricated massacre.

chapters.title: The Long Route Home
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Running silent toward the Authority's broadcast spire, she is boarded by Odile, who defects at last and gives her the master key — and the truth that the nine-second gravity failure was the Authority testing a weapon to erase dissenting memories system-wide. Beat: desperate alliance, clock now audible.

chapters.title: Customs
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Captured at the spire, she faces the Director — her father — who offers restoration, family, power, if she surrenders the chip. He genuinely loves her, which makes it worse. Beat: temptation at full strength; power offered as love, corruption wearing a father's face.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix, climax. She triggers the broadcast from inside the spire as the memory-weapon charges; the truth floods every screen in the system while the weapon fires and takes her stored memories with it — including, she suspects, pieces of herself she wanted to keep. Beat: sacrifice as self-erasure; justice paid for in identity.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Carried Nothing
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix, months later, memory-partially-restored by Elio and Sena's testimony. The war is over; the Authority stands trial in the first court both worlds built together. Beatrix runs honest cargo now, carrying nothing illegal — and finally free. Beat: quiet resolution; identity rebuilt not from what was taken but from what she chose.
